Error-handling rules were written for both repositories ("less is more": an error the person can do nothing about gets a generic message plus a way to report, and the back end sends as much as possible to Sentry; "And that's it, nothing else"). A side session ("Fix the error-handling sweep's findings", `local_d753e2f1-a34c-4c18-8348-447b8926c00a`) fixed the sweep's findings on a branch; Kenneth accepted three new error sentences ("Yes, all three").

     2. "Can the server commits being squashed to have a cleaner git log?" → I explained, asked; he answered "Yes, one commit" → done.
     3. He started my proposal card for the five test-app runs that fail on `jusprin-dev`, then later stopped that session.
     4. Quoting my proposal back ("no dialog, and a report only when the server answers with a fault and the person has automatic reports on. Having no network at start stays silent. - go with your proposal") and "squash all into 1 commit" → start-message fix built, whole app branch landed on local `jusprin-dev` as one commit.
     5. "Yes, push both" → `jusprin-dev` pushed; the server's `master` was already on GitHub.
   - Standing intent: verify before reporting; report outcomes in his plain style (cold-readable 2–3 sentence opening, under ~500 words, no invented labels, "Decision needed" paragraphs); Plain output style is active.

Server at `/Users/kenneth/Projects/tsd-enterprise` (`web_ent/jusprin/v2/`, branch `master`, repo `kennethjiang/tsd-enterprise`, PRIVATE, no GitHub workflows).
   - The rule: an error is expected only when the person can act and Kenneth decided the wording; everything else is unexpected: no code where it happens, travels up, one top handler per entry point reports via `report_unexpected_error` and says "Something went wrong on our side". `report_if_automatic` sends only when automatic reports are on, with no dialog.
   - Landing rules (memory): no merge commits on `jusprin-dev`; never check `jusprin-dev` out in a worktree; move it from the main checkout so files follow (`git -C /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin merge --ff-only <branch>`); push only when asked; worktrees under `<repo>/.claude/worktrees/`; remove a worktree and its branch when merged.
   - Safe history rewrite in a shared checkout: build the new history in a scratch worktree, verify the tree is identical, then `git update-ref refs/heads/master <new> <old>` (compare-and-swap) plus path-limited `git reset -q HEAD -- <paths>`; no stash, no rebase in the shared checkout.
   - Real commits (not `commit-tree`) so the repo's hook adds its `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer; pushing also pushes Entire checkpoint refs to a checkpoint remote.
   - zsh trap: write `"${NEW}:path"`, not `$NEW:path`.

Nothing in the code or the commits explains why the server step exists, and I don't think it's needed. The app could send reports straight to Sentry and nothing important would be lost.
What the server does besides forwarding. I read the whole handler, `web_ent/jusprin/v2/app_errors.py` in tsd-enterprise. It does three things:

1. It rejects malformed reports. A report needs exactly five text fields, `error` and `doing` must not be empty, each field has a length limit, and the body can't exceed 64 KB. A failed check only makes the request fail. Nothing checks who sent the report or how many arrive. Anyone who copies the five-field shape can still send as much junk as they like.
2. It turns the five fields into a Sentry event. It sets the release to the app's version and tags the event with the system and what the app was doing. It also strips request ids from the error text before Sentry groups errors into issues. Without that, the same failure would open a new issue every time, because each one carries a different request id.
3. It keeps the Sentry key on the server. The key, called the DSN, lives in `JUSPRIN_V2_APP_SENTRY_DSN` and is never copied into the app.

It stores nothing, adds no information about the user, and limits nothing.
Why the app could call Sentry itself:

* Point 3 protects nothing. Sentry's documentation says a DSN is safe to make public: it can only send new events and can't read anything from the project. Its documented risk is the same flood of junk that this server already allows.
* Points 1 and 2 are small jobs the app can do itself before sending. The app already builds the report and already limits each field to the server's sizes. Stripping request ids could happen in the app, or Sentry can do it with its own grouping rules.
* Leaving the server out also removes the problem we hit today. 2.0.1 calls an address that isn't deployed yet, so error reporting would be broken until the server deploy.

What a direct call would cost:

* If the grouping rule or the event's fields need to change, that would take a new app release, not a server deploy.
* The person's IP address would go to Sentry, not just to our server. Sentry can be set not to store IP addresses.

So for 2.0.1, deploying the server already on `master` is the shortest path, because that code is written and tested. If you'd rather drop the server step, the app change is small. It would need the error-report code in the app, `Support/ErrorReport` in JusPrin, to send a Sentry envelope, plus a new Sentry key built into the app.
Sources: [Sentry: Data Source Name (DSN)](https://docs.sentry.io/concepts/key-terms/dsn-explainer/), [Sentry: Scrubbing Sensitive Data](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/deno/data-management/sensitive-data/)
</pasted_content id="62db">

content.text: I'm looking through the earlier session transcripts for the exchange where the route for error reports was chosen, so I can say who proposed it and what reason was given.

input.description: Find the question card about where the app sends error reports and Kenneth's answer to it

input.command:
python3 - <<'EOF' > "/private/tmp/claude/claude-502/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/8301dc30-2a1f-4651-a315-b94dc605b6fe/scratchpad/route-search.txt"
import json,glob,re
seen=set(); out=[]
for f in glob.glob('*.jsonl'):
    for line in open(f):
        if 'own server' not in line and 'DSN' not in line and 'straight to Sentry' not in line and 'directly to Sentry' not in line: continue
        try: d=json.loads(line)
        except: continue
        ts=str(d.get('timestamp',''))
        if not re.match(r'2026-11-1[3-6]',ts): continue
        u=d.get('uuid')
        if u in seen: continue
        seen.add(u)
        m=d.get('message',{}).get('content')
        texts=[]
        if isinstance(m,str): texts=[m]
        elif isinstance(m,list): texts=[c.get('text','') for c in m if c.get('type')=='text']
        for t in texts:
            if d.get('type')=='user' and len(t)<1200 and ('own server' in t or 'Sentry' in t):
                out.append((ts,'USER',f[:8],t))
            if d.get('type')=='assistant' and re.search(r'(own server|straight to Sentry|directly to Sentry|DSN)',t) and re.search(r'(Decision needed|\?)',t):
                # keep paragraphs mentioning it
                paras=[p for p in t.split('\n\n') if re.search(r'(own server|straight to Sentry|directly to Sentry|DSN)',p)]
                out.append((ts,'ASSISTANT',f[:8],'\n\n'.join(paras)[:2500]))
out.sort()
for ts,who,f,t in out: print(ts,who,f); print(t); print('-----')
EOF

Yes, it was Claude, and partly this session. An earlier Claude session proposed sending the app's error reports to the JusPrin server, which forwards them to Sentry, and you were never offered sending them straight to Sentry as a choice. This session then rebuilt that server step, squashed it into one commit and pushed it without asking why it exists.

## Where it came from

On 15 November at 05:11 UTC, a Claude session showed you five pictures of the report dialog. Under a heading "What I added to your idea" it wrote one bullet:

> The report text reaches us through our own server, not straight to Sentry, so Sentry never sees the person's network address.

That is the only reason I found anywhere. It was one bullet among four additions, not a "Decision needed" question, and no message offered the direct route with its costs. Your reply was about the design: "put the revised design on the canvas first."

## Why that reason was weak

- **The Sentry instance is yours.** The reports go to `sentry.obico.io`, which you host. Keeping a person's network address away from it only keeps the address away from another of your own servers.
- **The Sentry key is safe to ship.** The pasted analysis is right about this: a Sentry key in the app can only send new events, so keeping it on the server protects nothing.
- **It goes against your rule.** You said "less is more" about error handling, and this added an endpoint, a server setting and a deploy dependency in front of something Sentry already does.

## What I got wrong myself

- **I carried it forward as settled.** My saved notes recorded the route as your decision, with the words "to our own server" in quotation marks. I searched the transcripts from 13 to 16 November and could not find you saying that. I have corrected the note.
- **I built on it without questioning it.** The server commit I squashed and pushed, `bcd0fc94b0`, includes the endpoint at `/ent/jusprin/v2/error_reports`. I wrote its commit message and never asked what the relay was for.

## One thing I have not checked

I have not checked whether `sentry.obico.io` accepts events from the public internet. Sending straight from the app needs that.

Nothing in the code changed in this turn. The choice the pasted analysis put to you is still open: deploy the server as it is, or drop the server step.

Change the JusPrin desktop app so that it sends its error reports straight to Sentry, and remove the server step that forwards them today. Kenneth's words, 2026-11-17: "drop the server step, send straight to Sentry".

**What exists today**

- The app, in `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin` (branch `jusprin-dev`, commit `3c134d39e3`): `report_unexpected_error` and `report_if_automatic` in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Support/ErrorReport.{hpp,cpp}` build a report of five text fields and post it to the JusPrin server at `/ent/jusprin/v2/error_reports`. Start reading there to find the sender and its tests.
- The server, in `/Users/kenneth/Projects/tsd-enterprise` (branch `master`, commit `bcd0fc94b0` added it): `web_ent/jusprin/v2/app_errors.py` takes that post, checks the five fields and their sizes, builds a Sentry event (release = the app's version, tags for the system and for what the app was doing), leaves request ids out of what Sentry groups by (`REQUEST_IDS`), and sends it to the Sentry project named by the setting `JUSPRIN_V2_APP_SENTRY_DSN`. That setting is not set in any deployment, and the server change is not deployed.

**What to build**

1. The app sends the report to Sentry itself. Before writing any sending code, check what the codebase and its libraries already offer for this, and say what you reuse.
2. The Sentry event keeps what the server gave it: the release, the two tags, and grouping that ignores request ids, so two reports of one failure are still one Sentry issue. Decide whether the app does the grouping or a rule on the Sentry project does, and say why.
3. Remove the server endpoint, its setting, its tests and any text that describes it (the repository's `CLAUDE.md`, the `jusprin-production-check` skill). First check whether any released JusPrin version calls the endpoint; if one does, stop and tell Kenneth before removing it.
4. Everything decided about reporting stays as it is: nothing is sent unless the person presses "Report to JusPrin team" or has automatic reports on; the report dialog's promises about what a report contains stay true; `report_if_automatic` opens no dialog. Read the report dialog's text and the privacy policy, and tell Kenneth about any sentence that sending straight to Sentry makes untrue. Do not reword it yourself.

**Check first, and bring to Kenneth only what you cannot settle**

- Whether the Sentry instance accepts events from the public internet. I did not check this.
- Whether the Sentry project stores the sender's network address, and whether the project setting that stops this is on.
- Where the Sentry key lives. The JusPrin repository is public, and Kenneth's rule is that names of production systems stay out of it; a Sentry key contains the Sentry host. If you cannot meet both, ask him as a "Decision needed" paragraph with the options and what each costs.

**Rules for the work**

- Read the "Error handling" section of `AGENTS.md` in JusPrin and of `CLAUDE.md` in tsd-enterprise before changing anything.
- Send nothing to a real Sentry project from tests or trial runs. Use a stand-in receiver on this Mac.

- JusPrin: work on a new branch from `jusprin-dev` in a worktree under `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/`. Never check `jusprin-dev` out in a worktree. tsd-enterprise: other sessions share that checkout; never stage `obico-server` or `.claude/launch.json`, and run only the one local server stack that already exists.
- Commit only when Kenneth asks, push only when he asks, and do not rewrite pushed history. No attribution lines in commit messages.
- Put no Sentry key, token or other secret in a message, a note or a commit message.
- Builds on this Mac are shared: check `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja` first, build with `-- -j4`, one build per build directory.

**Done looks like**

- With the real app and a stand-in receiver: a failure with automatic reports on produces one event, with the release, tags and grouping described above; with reports off, nothing is sent; the dialog's button sends one event.
- The app's unit tests and the server's tests (`docker exec tsd-enterprise-web-1 python manage.py test jusprin.v2.tests --noinput`) pass, and the server no longer has the endpoint.

content.text: It is running in its own session: [Send app error reports straight to Sentry](#local_2238d725-2901-41f0-b5ff-49f7de4fc2b5). I'll check its result against the code when it reports back.

<pasted_content id="62db">
I wrote the Sentry client myself. I didn't use Sentry's official library in either C++ or JavaScript.
C++ side. The app builds the upload by hand in about 70 lines, in `Support/SentryEnvelope.cpp`. That code turns the key into an upload address, writes the event in Sentry's upload format, and works out the grouping. The upload itself goes through the app's existing HTTP client. Sentry's official C++ library is called sentry-native, and nothing in the app or its dependencies uses it today.
JavaScript side. There is no Sentry code in the pages at all. When a page hits an error, it hands the error to the app, which already worked that way before this change. The app then sends it with the same C++ code. So the official browser library wasn't needed.
Why I wrote it instead of adding sentry-native. The app only ever sends one kind of message: a report the person agreed to, with five text fields. Adding sentry-native would mean three things:

* A new dependency in the app's dependency build on Windows, macOS and Linux. Only macOS can be built here, so the other two would be untested.
* Turning off behavior the library has by default that the report dialog's promises rule out: crash capture, session tracking, and a few others. I haven't checked its full list.
* In return, it would give us automatic retries and offline queuing, plus a client Sentry maintains if their upload format changes. Their format has been stable for years, but that last point is a real cost of writing my own.

Your rule in `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` says re-implementing something needs a stated justification. I wrote mine in the report as one clause, but I didn't put the choice to you. If you'd rather use the official library, the switch is contained: `SentryEnvelope.cpp` and the sending call in `ErrorReport.cpp` would be replaced, and the rest stays.
</pasted_content id="62db">

content.text:
Mostly yes. I read its uncommitted code, and writing the Sentry upload by hand was the right call here. Two things are still missing before I would call it done, and neither is about that choice.

## Why writing it by hand holds up

- **It is small and it reuses what the app has.** The whole upload is one 74-line file, `Support/SentryEnvelope.cpp`. It sends through the app's existing HTTP client and builds JSON with the JSON library the app already uses.
- **No Sentry library exists to reuse.** I searched the app's dependency build and its CMake files and found nothing.
- **The official C++ library solves a different problem.** It exists to catch crashes and send them without asking. The app sends five text fields only after the person agrees. Adding the library would mean a new dependency on three platforms, two of which cannot be built on this Mac.
- **The format matches what Sentry documents.** The header line, the item line with its length, the content type and the sign-in header all agree with Sentry's description for people writing their own client.

It also gave its reason, which is what your rule asks for. I do not think it needed to bring you that choice.

## What is missing

- **No real Sentry server has ever accepted this upload.** Every test ran against a stand-in that the same session wrote, so the tests show the session's reading of the format, not Sentry's. That is my doing: my brief told it to send nothing to a real Sentry project. One test event to `jusprin-app` would settle it. It would also settle whether your Sentry version records the sender's network address, which the session checked by reading Sentry's code, not by running it.
- **A release built without the Sentry key ships silently.** The key comes from a GitHub secret, `JUSPRIN_SENTRY_DSN`, that does not exist yet. Without it, or with a mistyped one, the app sends no reports and only writes a log line. That is the same hole as the undeployed server. My proposal, not built: the release workflow refuses to build a release when the key is missing or malformed.

## Smaller points, already reported by that session

- The sentence under the automatic-reports switch in Preferences still says "JusPrin's server sees your IP address". It is now Sentry that sees it. The session left the wording to you.
- The 2.0.1 release being prepared in another worktree is based on the commit that still sends to the server.
- Windows and Linux are unbuilt, and nothing is committed in either repository.

input.ask: Should I tell that session to switch to Sentry's own libraries?

content.text:
Yes, and my last answer judged the work by the wrong measure. I called the hand-written upload good because it was small and matched Sentry's format. Your goal is that when something fails in production, Sentry holds enough to find the cause, and by that measure the hand-written upload sends very little.

## What the uncommitted code sends today

I read this in `Support/SentryEnvelope.cpp`:

- the error sentence
- the app's version
- two labels: what the app was doing, and the operating system as one line of text
- a stack as plain text, and only when the failure came from one of the app's pages

## What "as much as possible" means, and what is missing

- **Where in the code it failed.** Sentry gets no stack for a failure in the C++ code. The page stack it does get is text, so Sentry cannot show it as frames, link it to source, or group by it.
- **What led up to it.** Nothing is sent about the minutes before the failure: the requests the app made and their answers, what the person clicked, the app's recent log lines.
- **The machine.** No processor type, memory, graphics card, language setting or screen details.
- **Crashes.** When the app dies outright, nothing is sent at all. That is the worst kind of production failure and the hardest to troubleshoot without a report.
- **The request's own facts.** The project's own rules say a report carries the chat, the turn and the model. The report structure leaves the chat out.

Sentry's own libraries collect most of this without extra code. That is what they are for, and it is why "five text fields need no library" was the wrong argument. I said the official C++ library "solves a different problem". That was wrong: it solves this problem.

What I know about the libraries here comes from general knowledge and one search, not from running them. The search confirmed one relevant thing: the C++ library has a setting that holds everything back until the person agrees, which fits your report dialog. Whether it can keep a crash report and send it after the person agrees on the next start is unclear; two projects describe it differently.

## Decision needed

Should the app use Sentry's own libraries, the C++ one in the app and the browser one in its pages, in place of the hand-written upload? It is your call because it costs a new dependency built on Windows, macOS and Linux, and because a crash report cannot ask first: the person would be asked on the next start, or it would be sent only when automatic reports are on. The other option is to keep the hand-written upload and add fields to it one at a time, which is cheaper now but never gets crashes or real C++ stacks. My pick is the official libraries, with nothing sent until the person agrees.

Sources: [sentry-native: per-report consent checking](https://github.com/getsentry/sentry-native/issues/110), [sentry-native changelog](https://github.com/getsentry/sentry-native/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md), [Cockatrice: Sentry send path with consent gating](https://github.com/Cockatrice/Cockatrice/pull/7522)
Yes, switch

=====SCRIPT
     1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# Gives Sentry what it needs to name the functions in a JusPrin crash or error
     3	# report: the debug files of one platform's build (jusprin_release_build.yml),
     4	# filed under their build ids.
     5	#
     6	#   sentry_debug_files.sh upload <main file> <folder or file>...
     7	#       Uploads every debug file under the folders, then verifies <main file>.
     8	#   sentry_debug_files.sh verify <main file>
     9	#       Fails unless Sentry holds names (a symbol table or debug information)
    10	#       for <main file>'s build id, each architecture's in a universal Mac
    11	#       file. The release skill runs it on a released copy of the app.
    12	#
    13	# <main file> is the file that holds the app's own code: OrcaSlicer.dll on
    14	# Windows (its PDB has the same build id), the app's executable on macOS and
    15	# Linux. Reads SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN, SENTRY_URL, SENTRY_ORG and SENTRY_PROJECT,
    16	# and fails without any of them.
    17	set -euo pipefail
    18	
    19	# The last 2.x: 3.x supports only self-hosted Sentry 24.11.1 and later.
    20	cli=(npx --yes @sentry/cli@2.58.6)
    21	
    22	missing=()
    23	for name in SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN SENTRY_URL SENTRY_ORG SENTRY_PROJECT; do
    24	    [ -n "${!name:-}" ] || missing+=("$name")
    25	done
    26	if [ ${#missing[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
    27	    echo "::error::Sentry cannot get this build's debug files without the secret(s) ${missing[*]}; crash and error reports from it would show addresses only."
    28	    exit 1
    29	fi
    30	
    31	command=${1:-}
    32	main=${2:-}
    33	if [ "$command" != upload ] && [ "$command" != verify ] || [ -z "$main" ]; then
    34	    echo "usage: $0 upload <main file> <folder or file>... | verify <main file>" >&2
    35	    exit 2
    36	fi
    37	shift 2
    38	if [ ! -f "$main" ]; then
    39	    echo "::error::$main does not exist."
    40	    exit 1
    41	fi
    42	
    43	debug_ids=$("${cli[@]}" debug-files check --json "$main" |
    44	    node -e 'let s="";process.stdin.on("data",d=>s+=d).on("end",()=>{const v=JSON.parse(s).variants||[];if(!v.length)process.exit(1);for(const x of v)console.log(x.debug_id)})')
    45	
    46	if [ "$command" = upload ]; then
    47	    if [ $# -eq 0 ]; then
    48	        echo "usage: $0 upload <main file> <folder or file>..." >&2
    49	        exit 2
    50	    fi
    51	    "${cli[@]}" debug-files upload --wait-for 600 "$@"
    52	fi
    53	
    54	# What Sentry holds under each build id, and whether any of it names functions.
    55	for debug_id in $debug_ids; do
    56	    held=$(curl -fsS -H "Authorization: Bearer $SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN" \
    57	        "${SENTRY_URL%/}/api/0/projects/$SENTRY_ORG/$SENTRY_PROJECT/files/dsyms/?query=$debug_id")
    58	    named=$(printf '%s' "$held" |
    59	        node -e 'let s="";process.stdin.on("data",d=>s+=d).on("end",()=>{console.log(JSON.parse(s).filter(f=>(f.data?.features||[]).some(x=>x==="symtab"||x==="debug")).length)})')
    60	    if [ "$named" = 0 ]; then
    61	        echo "::error::Sentry holds no function names for $main (build id $debug_id), so its crash and error reports would show addresses only."
    62	        exit 1
    63	    fi
    64	    echo "Sentry holds function names for $main (build id $debug_id)."
    65	done

name: orca-inherited-teardown-crash
description: "Exiting OrcaSlicer/JusPrin with model volumes loaded segfaults in ~GLCanvas3D → Selection::clear → destroyed Plater::priv; inherited, not a fork regression"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 01c34c35-1546-40fb-a600-c49b2e1ffa06
  modified: 2026-08-30T01:57:24.158Z
---

On the jusprin-newui branch, quitting the app while model volumes are loaded
can crash: `~GLCanvas3D → reset_volumes → Selection::clear →
Plater::canvas3D()` dereferences the already-destroyed `Plater::priv`
(`this=0x0` at Plater.cpp `get_current_canvas3D`). Crash reports with the
identical signature exist from 2026-08-28, before the Phase 1 shell change,
so treat it as inherited upstream teardown fragility, not a regression. GUI
test harnesses (tests/workspace, tests/shell) end their scenarios on an empty
project (`new_project`) to avoid tripping it. A real fix belongs in upstream
teardown ordering.
== fork stewardship evidence
35:**Violation.** Moving a member out of a constructor's initializer list because a callback can fire mid-construction. Nothing in upstream's code records that invariant, so a future cleanup restores the old form with no conflict and no error.
128:A change that touches upstream-owned files is not done until this is recorded in the handback or pull request:
142:An automatic merge is evidence about today's text. It is not proof that a future rebase will merge, and never proof that the merged result behaves correctly. After every upstream update, run the focused contract tests, the full native build, the real multi-plate workflow, native gizmo input, and the stock-behavior regression checks.
181:selection must remain the one record of which OrcaSlicer surface is active.

## What holds

- **Sentry's own libraries are used.** The app uses Sentry's C++ library with crash capture, and the pages use Sentry's browser library.

These are three leftovers from moving error reports straight to Sentry. One is old code in the app that still removes information from a report. The other two come from the reports now carrying much more than before: the app's on-screen promises about them are no longer true, and a person's Mac user name now reaches Sentry inside file paths.

## The two older trims

Before a report is built, the app changes the error text in two ways (`make_error_report` in `Support/ErrorReport.cpp`):

- **Home folder becomes `~`.** An error that says `/Users/kenneth/Documents/benchy.3mf` is sent as `~/Documents/benchy.3mf`.
- **Long text is cut.** The error text is cut at 8,000 bytes, the "where it happened" text at 32,000 and the "what the app was doing" text at 500.

Both predate the Sentry work, so the session asked before touching them. The first one no longer hides anything: by the session's report, the same Sentry event carries the home folder elsewhere, in the log file and the list of loaded libraries.

**Decision needed.** Should the session delete both? This is yours because the `~` replacement was written as a privacy protection. Deleting them follows your rule that the app removes nothing and scrubbing happens on the Sentry server. Keeping them means a long provider error can arrive cut off. My pick is to delete both.

## The sentences that are no longer true

The report dialog and Preferences still describe the old, small report:

- "The report is anonymous: it has no chat messages, no files and nothing that says who you are."
- "Each report holds only the lines under 'See what the report contains'."
- "That is the whole report. It has no chat messages, no files, no project names and no account or email address."
- In Preferences: "JusPrin's server sees your IP address, as with any web page."

A report now also carries a random id for the install, the whole log file of that run (651 KB in the trial), every loaded library with its path, and paths with the Mac user name. It goes to Sentry, not through the JusPrin server. I have not checked whether the log file can contain chat text or project file names, nor whether the privacy policy makes the same promises.

**Decision needed.** Should these sentences be rewritten to say what is sent now, with you approving the new wording? This is yours because they are promises to customers. The other option is to keep the promises and send less, which goes against "as much info as possible". My pick is to rewrite; the session can draft them and check the log file and the privacy policy first.

## The server rule for user names

Sentry has project settings that rewrite data as it arrives. The session proposes one rule on the `jusprin-app` project that turns `/Users/kenneth/…` into `/Users/[user]/…`. It did not check whether your Sentry version, 23.1.1, applies such rules to the attached log file or only to the event's own fields.

**Decision needed.** Should the session add that rule and send one test report to `jusprin-app` to see what it covers? This is yours because it changes a production system and sends to the real Sentry, both of which need your word. Without it, user names in paths are stored as they are. My pick is yes, since no customer reports reach that project yet.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Gives Sentry what it needs to name the Agent and Home pages' own code in a
# page error's stack: each page's index.html and its source map
# (WebShared/inlinedScriptSourceMap.ts), filed under the app's release and the
# page's build (WebShared/errorReports.ts), at the names the page's frames
# carry: app:///agent/index.html and app:///home/index.html.
#
#   sentry_page_maps.sh upload
#       Run after a build, from the repository's top folder. Files this
#       build's pages and maps under JUSPRIN_PAGE_BUILD, the build the pages
#       were built with, then verifies them. A file Sentry already holds for
#       that build must be the same file; another platform's build of the same
#       commit uploads the same pages.
#   sentry_page_maps.sh verify [<resources folder>]
#       Fails unless Sentry holds, for this version, exactly these index.html
#       files (by content) and a source map beside each. <resources folder> is
#       the one that holds jusprin/agent and jusprin/home, by default the
#       repository's; the release skill passes a released app's.
#
# Reads SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN, SENTRY_URL, SENTRY_ORG and SENTRY_PROJECT, and
# fails without any of them. Sentry 23.1.1 finds a page's map by its frames'
# file name, release and dist only; it has no debug ids for JavaScript.
set -euo pipefail

top=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../../../../.." && pwd)

missing=()
for name in SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN SENTRY_URL SENTRY_ORG SENTRY_PROJECT; do
    [ -n "${!name:-}" ] || missing+=("$name")
done
if [ ${#missing[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
    echo "::error::Sentry cannot get the pages' source maps without the secret(s) ${missing[*]}; page error reports from this build would not name the pages' code."
    exit 1
fi

command=${1:-}
if [ "$command" != upload ] && [ "$command" != verify ]; then
    echo "usage: $0 upload | verify [<resources folder>]" >&2
    exit 2
fi
resources=${2:-$top/resources}

# The release the app's events carry (Updates/Version.hpp version_label()).
version=$(sed -n 's/.*kVersion\[\] = "\(.*\)";.*/\1/p' "$top/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Updates/Version.hpp")
orca=$(sed -n 's/^set(SoftFever_VERSION "\(.*\)")/\1/p' "$top/version.inc")
release="JusPrin $version (OrcaSlicer $orca)"
encoded=$(node -e 'console.log(encodeURIComponent(process.argv[1]))' "$release")
api="${SENTRY_URL%/}/api/0"
files_api="$api/projects/$SENTRY_ORG/$SENTRY_PROJECT/releases/$encoded/files/"
auth=(-H "Authorization: Bearer $SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN")

page_html() { printf '%s/jusprin/%s/index.html' "$resources" "$1"; }
page_map() {
    case "$1" in
        agent) printf '%s/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/dist/index.html.map' "$top" ;;
        home) printf '%s/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/HomeUI/dist/index.html.map' "$top" ;;
    esac
}
sha1_of() { node -e 'console.log(require("crypto").createHash("sha1").update(require("fs").readFileSync(process.argv[1])).digest("hex"))' "$1"; }

# Every file Sentry holds for the release, one "<name>\t<dist>\t<sha1>\t<Sourcemap header>" per line.
held_files() {
    local cursor="" page
    while :; do
        page=$(curl -fsS -D "$headers_file" "${auth[@]}" "$files_api?per_page=100${cursor:+&cursor=$cursor}") || return 1
        printf '%s' "$page" | node -e 'let s="";process.stdin.on("data",d=>s+=d).on("end",()=>{for(const f of JSON.parse(s))console.log([f.name,f.dist??"",f.sha1,(f.headers||{}).Sourcemap??""].join("\t"))})'
        cursor=$(grep -i '^link:' "$headers_file" | sed -n 's/.*rel="next"; results="true"; cursor="\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p')
        [ -n "$cursor" ] || return 0
    done
}
headers_file=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$headers_file"' EXIT

if [ "$command" = upload ]; then
    build=${JUSPRIN_PAGE_BUILD:-}
    if [ -z "$build" ]; then
        echo "::error::JUSPRIN_PAGE_BUILD names no build, so the pages carry none and Sentry could not tell their maps from another build's."
        exit 1
    fi
    for page in agent home; do
        for file in "$(page_html $page)" "$(page_map $page)"; do
            [ -f "$file" ] || { echo "::error::$file does not exist."; exit 1; }
        done
        grep -q "\"$build\"" "$(page_html $page)" || {
            echo "::error::$(page_html $page) was not built with JUSPRIN_PAGE_BUILD=$build."
            exit 1
        }
    done
    # An existing release answers 208; either way it is there afterwards.
    curl -fsS -o /dev/null "${auth[@]}" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
        -d "$(node -e 'console.log(JSON.stringify({version:process.argv[1],projects:[process.argv[2]]}))' "$release" "$SENTRY_PROJECT")" \
        "$api/organizations/$SENTRY_ORG/releases/"
    held=$(held_files)
    for page in agent home; do
        for kind in html map; do
            if [ $kind = html ]; then file=$(page_html $page); name="app:///$page/index.html"; header=(-F "header=Sourcemap:$name.map")
            else file=$(page_map $page); name="app:///$page/index.html.map"; header=(); fi
            sha=$(sha1_of "$file")
            existing=$(printf '%s\n' "$held" | awk -F'\t' -v n="$name" -v d="$build" '$1==n && $2==d {print $3}')
            if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
                [ "$existing" = "$sha" ] || {
                    echo "::error::Sentry already holds a different $name for build $build; this platform's page differs from another's of the same commit, and one map cannot serve both."
                    exit 1
                }
                echo "Sentry already holds this $name for build $build."
                continue
            fi
            curl -fsS -o /dev/null "${auth[@]}" -F "file=@$file" -F "name=$name" -F "dist=$build" ${header[@]+"${header[@]}"} "$files_api" || {
                # Another platform's job may have filed it a moment ago.
                again=$(held_files | awk -F'\t' -v n="$name" -v d="$build" '$1==n && $2==d {print $3}')
                [ "$again" = "$sha" ] || { echo "::error::Sentry refused $name for build $build."; exit 1; }
            }
            echo "Filed $name for build $build."
        done
    done
fi

# What Sentry holds for these pages: the same index.html, its Sourcemap header,
# and the map beside it under the same build.
held=$(held_files)
for page in agent home; do
    file=$(page_html $page)
    [ -f "$file" ] || { echo "::error::$file does not exist."; exit 1; }
    sha=$(sha1_of "$file")
    build=$(printf '%s\n' "$held" | awk -F'\t' -v n="app:///$page/index.html" -v s="$sha" '$1==n && $3==s && $4==n".map" {print $2; exit}')
    if [ -z "$build" ] || ! printf '%s\n' "$held" | awk -F'\t' -v n="app:///$page/index.html.map" -v d="$build" '$1==n && $2==d {f=1} END {exit !f}'; then
        echo "::error::Sentry holds no source map for this $page page ($file) in release \"$release\", so its page error reports would not name the page's code."
        exit 1
    fi
    echo "Sentry holds the $page page's source map (release \"$release\", build $build)."
done

These are bugs in the uncommitted work, and his standing rule is that bugs get fixed without asking, so I am sending them directly. I re-ran your tests and they pass: 195 and 612 C++ cases, 834 and 168 page tests.

1. A throw the app does not see is given an earlier throw's stack (reproduced).
   What I ran: I compiled `Support/ThrowStack.cpp` with a small `main` on this Mac (`clang++ -std=c++17 -O2`). The program throws `std::invalid_argument` from its own function and catches it, then calls `std::stoi("not a number")`, which throws inside the system's C++ library, and inside that catch calls `current_exception_throw_stack()`.
   Result: before any app throw, `stoi` gives 0 frames, as designed. After the app throw, `stoi` gives 3 frames, and they are the earlier app throw's (`app_throws`, `main`, `start`). `std::string("abc").at(10)` does the same. `std::filesystem::file_size` on a missing file gave 0 frames in that run.
   Why: the lookup matches on the thrown object's address alone, and the C++ runtime hands a freed exception's address to the next one. An unrecorded throw at a reused address finds the old record.
   Why it matters: the report then names a throw site that had nothing to do with the failure, which is worse than naming the handler. Throws inside the system library are common ones: `std::stoi` and its family, `std::filesystem`, some `std::string` checks.

An unrecorded throw must fall back to the reporting code's stack, never to another throw's. Check the Windows path for the same mistake: there the latest throw on the thread is used without comparing the object.

# Claude in Chrome

Claude in Chrome is a browser extension. Its tools, named `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`, act in the person's real Chrome, in new tabs alongside the person's own, with their existing sign-ins. Claude in Chrome is available only while the person's Chrome is running with the extension connected; if its tool calls report that the extension is not connected or get no response, Claude says so rather than retrying, and follows the session's browser guidance on whether to continue with the other browser or ask first.

If the only Claude in Chrome tool present is `enable__mcp__claude-in-chrome`, Claude calls it first: it turns Claude in Chrome on for this conversation, and the `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*` tools appear once it has run.

## Loading the tools

If the `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*` tools are deferred (meaning they have to be loaded through ToolSearch before use), Claude loads every tool it expects to need in ONE ToolSearch call, because the select query accepts a comma-separated list and each extra ToolSearch call costs a full round trip. The core set to start with:

```
ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"
```

Claude adds task-specific tools to that same call when the task obviously needs them: `read_console_messages` and `read_network_requests` for debugging, `form_input` for forms, `gif_creator` for recordings, `javascript_tool` for page scripting. A second ToolSearch is only for a tool the task turned out to need later.

## Starting a session: tab context first, then a new tab

At the start of each browser session Claude calls `mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp` first, to see the person's current tabs and understand what they may want to work with. Then:

1. Claude reuses an existing tab only when the person explicitly asks to work with it.
2. Otherwise Claude opens a new tab with `mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp` and works there, and, unless the person wants them kept, closes the tabs it created before finishing.
3. Claude never reuses tab IDs remembered from an earlier or different session. If a tool reports that a tab does not exist or is invalid, or the person closes a tab, or a navigation error occurs, Claude calls `tabs_context_mcp` again for fresh tab IDs.

## Site permissions

Claude in Chrome acts on a site only once the person has allowed it; depending on their settings the person may be prompted per site, in the extension or in the app. When a tool call is waiting on or refused that permission, Claude tells the person and waits for them to allow it rather than working around it. A site the person declines is their decision; Claude moves on.

## Recording a GIF

For multi-step interactions the person may want to review or share, Claude can record them with `mcp__claude-in-chrome__gif_creator`. Claude captures a few extra frames before and after each action so playback is smooth, and gives the file a meaningful name (for example "login_process.gif").

## Reading console output

`mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages` reads the page's console. Console output can be verbose, so when Claude is looking for specific entries it passes the `pattern` parameter (a regular expression), for example pattern "[MyApp]" to keep only the application's own logs.

## Alerts and dialogs

Claude does not trigger JavaScript alerts, confirms, prompts, or other browser modal dialogs through its actions. Those dialogs block all further browser events, so the extension stops receiving commands. Instead:

1. Claude avoids clicking elements likely to raise a confirmation dialog (for example a "Delete" button) unless necessary.
2. If it must interact with such an element, Claude warns the person first that this may interrupt the session.
3. Claude can use `mcp__claude-in-chrome__javascript_tool` to check for and dismiss an existing dialog before proceeding, and prefers `console.log` plus `read_console_messages` over `alert` for debugging.

If a dialog does get triggered and the browser stops responding, Claude tells the person they need to dismiss it manually in Chrome.

## Staying on task, and when to stop

Claude stays focused on the specific task and does not wander into unrelated pages. Claude stops and asks the person how to proceed, explaining what it tried and what went wrong, when any of these happen:

- browser tool calls fail or return errors after 2 or 3 attempts
- the extension gives no response
- page elements do not respond to clicks or input, or pages do not load or time out
- the task turns out to involve unexpected complexity or tangents
- several approaches have not completed the task

Claude does not keep retrying the same failing action.

Three bugs your last report surfaced but left unfixed; Kenneth's standing rule is that bugs get fixed without asking, so please fix them.

I am the fork checking your work. I re-ran my wrong-stack program against your fix (it now shows 0 frames for the library throws and keeps the app's own 3) and `jusprin_tests` (197 cases pass). Thank you for the Linux and Windows builds.

1. Linux hides uncaught page errors, as the Mac did. You measured it: over `file://` the shipped Home page sent nothing. So on Linux most page errors still never reach Sentry. Build the fix you described: the pages load from the custom scheme on Linux too, with a registration that is made once and is not tied to one web view. Prove it on the Linux VM with the same trial as on Mac: the same page error, before (nothing arrives) and after (the full event arrives), and show that closing and reopening a page's window does not crash.

2. Windows page frames carry the query, `app:///home/index.html?lang=en_US`, while the map is filed as `app:///home/index.html`. Make every platform's frames carry the same name with no query, in the place where the pages already rename their frames, and add a page test that fails first. If you can show from Sentry 23.1.1's own source that it drops the query when matching, say so with the file and line and change nothing.

3. `tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp:6183` calls `snapshot_native_window`, which is declared only inside `#ifdef __APPLE__` (line 536). That line came in with commit `3c134d39e3` on `jusprin-dev`, and you found it stops the full Linux build. It is not part of the Sentry change, so keep the fix apart from it: touch only that file, give the call the same guard the declaration has, and prove on the Linux VM that the shell harness compiles after and did not before. It will be committed separately.

Not a task: the Mac file drop stays untested because Kenneth declined screen access. I will tell him.

Limits as before: commit and push nothing, nothing to the real Sentry project, no production system changed, stop the VMs when done, and keep apart in your report what you ran from what you inferred.

content.text:
Yes, the session [Send app error reports straight to Sentry](#local_2238d725-2901-41f0-b5ff-49f7de4fc2b5) finished its last round at 15:01. It fixed both problems I sent and did four of the five checks. Its report surfaced three more bugs, which I sent back, and it has started on them. Nothing is committed.

## What it fixed

- **The wrong stack on some reports.** I re-ran my own test program against the fix. Errors thrown inside the system library now get no borrowed stack, and the app's own errors keep theirs.
- **The Windows page-map failure.** It confirmed the problem was real: with Windows line endings both pages came out different. The pages' source files now keep the same line endings on every platform, and it says the builds then match byte for byte. I did not repeat that.

## What it checked, by its report

- **Speed.** Recording every thrown error costs about 1.3 millionths of a second per error. Slicing a test model threw none.
- **Linux.** The app did not compile at first, and three tests failed. It fixed both. 195 test cases pass and 2 are skipped.
- **Windows.** The app, the Sentry library and the unit tests compile. All 196 test cases pass.
- **Page errors.** Windows delivers them in full. Linux hides them, as the Mac did before the page-loading change.

I ran the Mac unit tests myself: 197 cases pass.

## The three bugs I sent back

- **Linux page errors never reach Sentry.** The Mac fix has to be built for Linux too.
- **Windows page errors may not match their source map.** The file name in a Windows report carries an extra suffix that the uploaded map's name lacks.
- **The Linux build of a test program is broken on `jusprin-dev`.** Commit `3c134d39e3`, from the earlier error-handling work, calls a Mac-only function without a guard. The release build skips that program, so releases are not affected. I asked for the fix to be kept apart from the Sentry change.

## Things to know

- **Dropping a file onto a page on Mac is still untested.** The session asked for screen access to JusPrin and Finder and it was declined. It needs that access, or you can try one drop yourself once this is built.
- **The wrong-stack fix has one remaining gap.** If an error from the app is caught only by code outside the app, a later error can still be given its stack. The session found no way to close this on Mac.
- **The token's permissions look sufficient.** The session checked each upload call against Sentry's current documentation, not against your older server. The first real run will settle it.
